claims.claim_ar: أَنَّ تُقْرَأُ بِفَتْحِ همزتها في القراءة العادية
claims.claim_en: The particle 'أَنَّ' is read with the hamza pronounced with a fatḥa in the ordinary reading.

claims.claim_ar: تَقْدِيرُ جملةِ «أَنَّ اللَّهَ...» هو «ذَلِكَ» (تقدير مُضمَر/مُستفاد لِأَنَّ)
claims.claim_en: The implied / supplied estimate (taqdīr) for the clause introduced by 'أَنَّ' is 'ذَلِكَ' (i.e. 'that'), meaning an understood reference like 'that (is because...)'.

claims.source_quote_ar: وَيُقْرَأُ بِغَيْرِ يَاءٍ، وَعَلَى الْأَلِفِ ضَمَّةٌ مُقَدَّرَةٌ
claims.claim_ar: اسم يَحْيَى (بِيَحْيَى) يجوز قراءته بدون ياء، وعلى الأَلِف تُقدَّر ضمّة (أي يُعطى رفعًا تقديريًا)، أو يُنطق بالياء المفتوحة بعد الألف في قراءة أخرى.
claims.claim_en: The name 'Yahya' (بِيَحْيَى) may be read without the final yā' (i.e. without pronouncing the yā') with an understood ḍamma on the alif (a suppletive case ending), or alternatively read with an explicit yā' after the alif in another reading.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited discussion in the source chunk explicitly treats the word "بُشْرَايَ" and its yāʾ/Alif behaviour; application to بِيَحْيَى in this verse is plausible by analogy but the chunk does not name يَحْيَى explicitly — verify whether al-Tibyan makes this claim for يَحْيَى in this verse or is speaking of a different lemma.
